title: Conversation Lab: facts, perspectives and next moves
idea: Refine the original workforce feedback candidate into an engaging first-time-team-lead practice experience. Use an invented missed-handoff story: a handoff note was absent on Monday, the next shift repeated a check, and the new lead has not yet heard the colleague’s account. Show a visual situation board that separates observed facts, possible explanations and missing context. Let the learner choose an opening and preview explicitly authored possible dialogue, not predicted human reactions. Reveal additional fictional context: the rota changed, the template was inaccessible to the colleague, and the expected owner was unclear. Learners can retain or revise their interpretation and their next move without a correct-answer score. Rehearse an observation, an invitation to hear the colleague’s account, and a feasible shared next step; couple each people action with the workflow support it depends on. A scenario agent should introduce a consequential objection or changed condition that changes a requirement. Produce a correctable before/after conversation plan and visible unresolved questions, not six empty reflection boxes. Provide a second optional fictional handoff situation with fewer suggestions as supported practice, not proof of transfer. Include a complete facilitated paper activity. The previous workforce journal is an immutable parent, not a measured baseline or approved intervention.
domain: Workforce learning and first-time team leadership
people: New team leads, colleagues, managers, learning teams and employee representatives; none participate in this demonstration.
constraints: No employee ranking, consequential HR advice, identifiable conversation recordings, profiling, telemetry, storage or network requests in the candidate. Use fictional inputs only; no real employee records. No simulated dialogue may be described as a prediction or evidence about real people. Make stopping, passing, uncertainty and dissent credible. At most two optional open-text fields on the main learner path; choices and concrete previews must carry the activity. Strong visual hierarchy, readable responsive layout, keyboard and focus support, exact proposal review/cancel, correction, cover/resume and confirmed complete handoff clearing. Put review metadata in Help rather than the primary learner flow. Non-AI facilitation must have complete materials. Product quality must be inspectable through role-originated requirements, rationale, interaction behavior, acceptance checks and evidence boundaries in the complete design brief. Participation and sharing are voluntary; protected time, staffing and workflow authority remain conditions to inspect. No human approval, field pilot, learning, transfer or flourishing evidence exists. Source preferably below 60000 bytes in the file-writing delivery; do not add a scientific calculator or reuse the school investigation.
